title: Check readings against boundary words and repo files before acceptance
summary: Retry of job 20261027-054206-w1y3 (dispatched, never verified, no findings recorded, so nothing to fix; the work is simply redone). Root cause: check_reading_acceptance in reading.rs validates only prior-result, evidence, survey and governance rules, never the reading's text against the boundary word list or its deliverables against files at HEAD. Add that deterministic check there, for the operator and later readers.

defaults_applied.how: New unit and wiring tests; fmt, clippy and test must pass.
The rule is enforced in code in check_reading_acceptance, not in prose.
Fixed at the acceptance gate for all readings, not for one job.
Criteria run tests that show refusal happening.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
One focused check added to one function.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs (check_reading_acceptance at ~2269 runs check_prior_result_and_scope, check_criteria_evidence, check_code_survey, check_governance_coverage in that order, and bails with a message on the first failure), crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs (boundary_scan, boundary_words, boundary_fragments), and crates/athena-core/Cargo.toml (athena-context is already a dependency). The new check goes last in that function and measures the reading's text directly with boundary_scan and its deliverable paths against the snapshot's file list at HEAD. No record or data file is added under crates/, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are not touched.
Job 20261027-054206-w1y3 is addressed by redoing its reading: it had no recorded findings. Deliverables and out_of_scope are kept the same as that job's.

check_reading_acceptance has no repo access today, so the producer passes it the set of paths at HEAD from the existing snapshot (athena_git::snapshot) and updates its callers; this may need a small change in lib.rs, which is why that file is listed.
briefs.rs changes only if boundary_scan needs a small public helper (e.g. a hit-word accessor); the word list itself is not changed.
Rule: a modify or delete deliverable for a path absent at HEAD is refused; a create deliverable for an existing path is refused. Paths are compared as repository-relative strings.
Past readings: the rule is new and refuses readings that name absent paths or banned words; expected 5% of newly refused readings.

acceptance_criteria.text: Root cause is named in the CHANGELOG.md entry and in a doc comment: reading output was checked only for prior-result, evidence, survey and governance rules, not against the boundary word list or repo files at HEAD. The check is called from check_reading_acceptance in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, not in a prompt file.

A unit test in reading.rs fails without the change and passes with it: a reading whose summary holds a boundary-scan word is refused and the error names the word. Run `cargo test -p athena-core reading`.

A unit test shows a 'modify' or 'delete' deliverable for a path absent at HEAD is refused, a 'create' deliverable for an existing path is refused, and a reading with valid paths and clean text is accepted. Run `cargo test -p athena-core reading`.
A test drives the reader path with the fake reader returning a bad reading and shows the reading is not accepted and the reason reaches the caller. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
Existing reading tests, including prior-result and scope tests, still pass; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` all pass.
The change refuses more readings and the higher refusal rate is intended: expected 5% of newly refused readings.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry saying readings are now checked against the boundary words and the repo's files, written for an outside reader.

out_of_scope: Re-implementing the disk-space hold, the hold-resume route, or the records-branch reader move from the earlier jobs
Editing prompt files, which have almost no token headroom
Semantic checks such as finding every reader of a moved path
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml or the workflows
Changing the boundary word list itself
departures: The change touches the acceptance gate and its callers, so cost and time lean slightly above the reference.
hard_reason: Adds a refusal rule to check_reading_acceptance, the gate that decides whether a reading is accepted, so a mistake would wrongly refuse or pass readings.
